notes:
Context: SMB support chatbot vendor that resells to small retailers. Self-serve signup; onboarding stalled due to latency complaints from EU merchant customers. They are currently defaulting to us-east region and have a client-side request timeout of 5s (React fetch).

Key pain: 'EU merchants are seeing slow replies and timeouts' — product lead says some customers get 1.5-3s median and occasional 7-9s tails which triggers UI retries. They think model choice might be the issue but primarily looks like region + prompt size problem.

Observed / diagnostic notes: 
- Frontend: default timeout 5s, no graceful retry/backoff. Client cancels requests and shows error to users.
- Backend: using hosted_api, single-region pin to us-east; no per-request region header in current integration.
- Prompts: sales-created canned responses include 800-1,200 token histories; lots of unnecessary system role repetition -> token bloat.
- Throughput: low concurrency now (SMB), but latency variance high when history >600 tokens.

Recommendations provided during call: 
1) Region test: run quick A/B switching to eu-west for EU-heavy merchants (use per-request region param) — expected p50 drop from ~1.5s to ~400-600ms.
2) Client timeout: increase client-side request timeout to 30s and implement streaming so UI can show progressive tokens and avoid user-side cancels.
3) Prompt guidance: implement summary-of-history approach — keep last 3 user messages + 250-token summarized system context; cap prompt window at ~600 tokens. Provide sample prompt templates we drafted.
4) Streaming & partial-render: enable streaming from Redwood hosted API to reduce perceived latency; demoed streaming on call.
5) Caching: recommend prefix caching for static instructions and reuse KV cache where repeated prompts occur.
6) Retry policy: exponential backoff on 5xx, do not retry on client-cancel.
7) Timeout / max_tokens: set server-side soft timeout 28s, max_tokens tuned to 256 for support replies to avoid tail spikes.

Customer quotes / color: 
- "We just want EU customers to feel snappy — if answers take >1s they complain." — Head of Product
- "We didn't realize our canned responses were adding so many tokens." — Engineering lead

Next steps (agreed): 
- AE (Jordan) to send perf tuning checklist + example prompt edits (today).
- SE (Avery) to run eu-west test by 2026-03-12 and share result table (p50/p95/p99).
- Customer to flip one EU merchant to eu-west staging and report UX metrics (time-to-first-token).
- If p50 improves as expected, propose rollout plan and recommend updating frontend timeout and enabling streaming.

Open questions / risks: 
- They may need SSO for business customers soon; could convert to higher tier.
- Some legacy merchants on slow mobile networks may still see tails; consider caching + prefetch strategies later.

Attachments & refs: pricing deck, perf checklist, sample prompts (links above).
